questions.question: What is the original name of the Empress of India Act and when was it instituted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__The Royal Titles Act of 1876__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• **The British Parliament approved **The Royal Titles Act 1876.** Queen Victoria was given the title of "The Empress of India"** under this Act. In that year, the Queen Victoria Proclamation was adopted. She had taken on this** title in 1876** with the support of** Benjamin Disraeli**, the** British Prime Minister.**
 
• **From 20 June 1837 until her passing in 1901**, Victoria ruled the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. Her 63-year and 7-month reign, also known as the **Victorian era.**
 
• The** reign of Queen Victoria **saw the growth of industry, advancements in education, the elimination of slavery, and improvements in **worker welfare.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of** Disraeli's well-known imperialist policies **was the** Royal Titles Act of 1876**. The British imperial title should only be used in India, it was agreed when the legislation was passed. As a result, it was first used by the** Queen in her signature in 1878**, and it first appeared on** British coins in 1893.**
 
• At the** Delhi Durbar in 1877**, she was given the formal title** Kaisar-i-Hind**, which means **"empress of India."**
 
• A** Royal Style and Titles Act**, also known as a Royal Titles Act, is an** Act of Parliament **passed in the relevant jurisdiction that establishes the formal title of the **sovereign there. **

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchases supplies from a supplier. The supplier sells 750 units of bags to the shopkeeper after gaining the sale price of 125 units of bags. What is the gain percentage of the supplier?
